analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md. The two supplied units are BASE text, lines 1629-2248 (head hunks at 872-878 and 1123-1183 fall outside them; a third range, 2098, is a one-line change in the Flint section). The visible patch excerpt is truncated, so I could only see the beginning of the performance and TTFT admission documentation. That text covers out-of-order observation freshness in EnginePerformanceMeasurements and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 rollback for the admission-rate estimators.

No code, configuration, authorization, crypto, or deployment behavior changes in this PR.

In the BASE excerpt, the documentation of native MiMo load/ownership, media ingress memory accounting, Flint tool and answer-stop constraints, and coordinator-serving channels contains no claim that weakens the threat model. The prefix-cache statements (MiMo SSD reuse, packed-prefix unsupported layouts) are consistent with T-041. They claim no change to the cache scope, TTL, HMAC lookup tags, or at-rest posture, and I found no new at-rest artifact or cross-tenant exposure introduced by wording.

The documented estimator changes concern availability and latency admission (T-010, T-029 territory) and keep physical admission and deadline checks. I cannot evaluate whether the code matches these docs; the truncated patch and the lack of the source files mean the new estimator behavior (a rollback env var that restores the previous estimators) is unverified.

Remaining integration question: if the full PR includes code changes to the admission estimators or measurement freshness, a reviewer should confirm that stale or out-of-order rate evidence cannot cause over-admission, or deadline bypass, for adversarial consumers. This documentation-only unit set gives no evidence of that.
